review.translation: [From these|0] [the coastland|2] [peoples|3] [spread out|1] [in their lands|4], [each|5] [with its own language|6], [according to their clans|7], [in their nations|8].

analysis.evidence: אֵלֶּה points back to the descendants just listed. With נִפְרְדוּ, the prefix מֵ marks the source from which the coastland peoples spread out.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition מִן appears as מֵ before א. אֵלֶּה is a common plural demonstrative pronoun.

analysis.evidence: מֵאֵלֶּה (“from these”) traces the coastland peoples back to the descendants just listed. The rest of the verse describes how those peoples spread out into their respective lands, each with its own language, grouped by clan and nation.
analysis.morphology: Niphal perfect, third person common plural. The initial נִ marks the Niphal stem, and the ending וּ agrees with the plural subject אִיֵּי הַגּוֹיִם.

draft.change: Add Genesis 10:5 as evidence for the use of אִי for a coastland’s inhabitants in the existing island-coastland sense.
draft.definition: An island or coastland, also used of the people who inhabit it.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:5 speaks of the coastlands of the nations spreading out, each person according to his language.

analysis.evidence: אִיֵּי הַגּוֹיִם means “the coastlands of the nations.” The verb נִפְרְדוּ describes the people spreading out, and בְּאַרְצֹתָם locates them “in their lands.” The coastlands here stand for their inhabitants.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew common noun, masculine plural construct. Its complement is הַגּוֹיִם, “the nations.”

analysis.evidence: The verse groups the peoples of the coastlands by land, language, and family, then calls them בְּגוֹיֵהֶם, “in their nations.”
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine plural common noun in the absolute state. The noun completes the construct phrase אִיֵּי הַגּוֹיִם, “the coastlands of the nations.”
analysis.sense: a people counted as a nation

analysis.evidence: The verse describes the dispersal of peoples. Their lands are listed alongside their languages, clans, and nations, so אֶרֶץ denotes the territories they inhabit.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ means “in.” The noun אֶרֶץ, of common gender, is plural construct with a third-person masculine plural possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אִישׁ לִלְשֹׁנוֹ, the masculine singular suffix on לִלְשֹׁנוֹ refers back to אִישׁ, giving the distributive reading “each according to his own language.”

אִישׁ gives the phrase its distributive force, “each according to his language.” The parallel references to their lands, clans, and nations identify language as another basis for distinguishing the peoples.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לִ־ means “according to.” The noun is singular, of common gender, and in the construct state before the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix וֹ, “his.”

analysis.evidence: Between לִלְשֹׁנוֹ (“according to his language”) and בְּגוֹיֵהֶם (“in their nations”), the phrase identifies the kinship groups into which these peoples were divided.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ means “according to.” The noun is feminine plural in the construct state and bears a third-person masculine plural possessive suffix, “their.”

analysis.evidence: After grouping the descendants by land, language and family, the verse identifies the nations to which they belong. The suffix הֶם refers to those descendants.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ introduces a masculine plural construct noun with the third-person masculine plural possessive suffix הֶם.
analysis.sense: a people counted as a nation
